quadrants.name: Platforms and protocols
quadrants.scope: Shared infrastructure, interfaces and wire protocols

rings.name: Adopt
rings.meaning: Use by default, because the evidence is consistent and the practice holds up at production scale.

rings.name: Trial
rings.meaning: Use on a real workload with an owner and an exit plan; sound, but not yet settled.

rings.name: Assess
rings.meaning: Study it and test it in isolation; it may matter, but evidence does not yet justify production use.

rings.name: Hold
rings.meaning: Avoid, and plan to retire where present; the evidence shows it fails, misleads or hides risk.

blips.name: Baseline before model
blips.summary: Measure a simple non-ML or single-call baseline first, and require any model or agent to beat it on the same task, metric and cost.

blips.name: Workflows before autonomous agents
blips.summary: Use the simplest design that works: a fixed workflow where steps are known, and open-ended agent control only where the task demonstrably needs it.

blips.name: Canary releases for model and prompt changes
blips.summary: Expose each model, prompt or configuration change to a small share of traffic against a control, with quality, latency and cost thresholds agreed before rollout.

blips.name: Blameless postmortems for AI incidents
blips.summary: Treat quality regressions, harmful outputs and agents acting out of scope as incidents, with written, blameless reviews that end in owned fixes and new evaluations.

blips.name: Problem-based requirements
blips.summary: Derive requirements from named customer problems through customer needs, so every AI capability traces to a problem it solves and unneeded requirements are cut.

blips.name: Feedback-loop mapping
blips.summary: Before scaling, draw the loops where a system's outputs return as its inputs, such as models trained on their own results, and name each delay and limit.

blips.name: Model cascades and routing
blips.summary: Send each request to the cheapest model that meets the quality bar and escalate only when needed; one study matched the best single model at up to 98% lower cost.

blips.name: Injection-resistant agent design patterns
blips.summary: Constrain what an agent can do after reading untrusted content, for example plan-then-execute. The patterns give provable resistance to prompt injection at an explicit cost in utility.

blips.name: Multi-agent decomposition
blips.summary: Splitting work across cooperating agents adds documented failure modes in system design, inter-agent misalignment and task verification. Test against a single agent or workflow before committing.

blips.name: Unbudgeted automatic retries
blips.summary: Agents and clients that retry without limits turn a slow dependency into overload. Cap retries with budgets and jittered backoff, and propagate deadlines through every step.

blips.name: W3C Trace Context across agent hops
blips.summary: Propagate one trace identifier through every agent, tool call, MCP server and queue, so a single request can be reconstructed end to end.

blips.name: OAuth to the current security BCP
blips.summary: Delegate agent access through OAuth as RFC 9700 recommends: audience-restricted, sender-constrained tokens. MCP authorization builds on OAuth, so the same baseline applies.

blips.name: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions
blips.summary: The open vocabulary for model, agent and tool telemetry. Instrument now, but every document is still in Development status: pin and record the version each service emits.

blips.name: Model Context Protocol
blips.summary: One open protocol for connecting AI applications to tools and data, now under Linux Foundation governance. Revisions still change: pin one and review its authorization section.

blips.name: Versioned open evaluation harness
blips.summary: Keep evaluations as versioned code in an open harness, so the same suite reruns unchanged on every model, prompt or vendor change and results stay comparable.

blips.name: Agent2Agent protocol
blips.summary: An open protocol for agents from different teams or vendors to discover each other and delegate tasks. Version 1.0 was released in March 2026; assess it where agents cross organisations.

blips.name: Telemetry only in a vendor's console
blips.summary: Agent telemetry that cannot be exported in open formats leaves traces split by vendor and ties cost and quality reporting to one tool. GN-0001 requires open conventions instead.

blips.name: Continuous quality evaluation in production
blips.summary: Offline evaluations missed production regressions in two public postmortems. Run quality evaluations continuously against live endpoints, and add each incident's failure as a new test.

blips.name: Cost reported with accuracy
blips.summary: Report every evaluation result with its cost per task. Accuracy alone has led to needlessly complex, costly agents and to wrong conclusions about what drives gains.

blips.name: Tail latency per agent step
blips.summary: Track p99 latency for each model and tool call and for the whole run. Rare slow calls come to dominate performance as agents chain more steps.

blips.name: Value-of-information measurement
blips.summary: Treat a measurement as reducing uncertainty for a named decision. Use the value of information to decide what to measure, including benefits called intangible.

blips.name: Answer-quality SLOs
blips.summary: Give each AI feature a quality indicator, such as graded acceptability on sampled traffic, with an explicit objective beside latency and availability.

blips.name: Repeated-trial reliability (pass^k)
blips.summary: Run each task several times and report the chance that all attempts succeed. Single-run success overstates the consistency customers will experience.

blips.name: LLM judges calibrated to human grades
blips.summary: Strong models can approximate human preference ratings, but show position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases. Use them at scale only with a versioned human-graded sample to check agreement.

blips.name: Cost and calls per completed task
blips.summary: Attribute token cost to each agent and workflow, and watch the distribution of model and tool calls per invocation to catch runaway loops before the invoice does.

blips.name: Task time horizons
blips.summary: Rates models by the length of task, in skilled human time, they complete half the time. Useful for scoping delegation; the measure is new and tied to software tasks.

blips.name: LLM judges without human calibration
blips.summary: Grading criteria drift as people review outputs, and LLM judges carry documented biases, including self-enhancement. Without a human-graded check, scores cannot be trusted to track quality.

blips.name: Benchmark scores as launch evidence
blips.summary: Public agent benchmarks often have inadequate holdouts and ignore cost, and single runs hide inconsistency; models with equally strong test scores can behave differently in deployment.

blips.name: NIST AI RMF and Generative AI Profile
blips.summary: A shared vocabulary for risk, legal and engineering: govern, map, measure and manage, with generative-AI risks such as confabulation. NIST has announced the framework is being revised.

blips.name: EU AI Act risk classification
blips.summary: Where the Act applies, classify each system against its risk tiers now: duties fall on deployers as well as providers, and obligations are phasing in.

blips.name: Model cards and datasheets
blips.summary: Keep a short, standard record for every deployed model and dataset: intended use, how it was evaluated, known gaps and uses that are out of scope.

blips.name: Per-agent identity and least privilege
blips.summary: Give each agent its own identity, the narrowest permissions its task needs and logged activity, as for any insider with access to important systems.

blips.name: OWASP Top 10 launch review
blips.summary: Map each LLM risk, from prompt injection to unbounded consumption, to a named control or an accepted risk before launch. The agentic list is newer and still settling.

blips.name: ISO/IEC 42001 AI management system
blips.summary: A certifiable management-system standard for AI, published 2023. Map existing controls to it first; certify where customers or regulators need independent assurance.

blips.name: AI impact assessment before build
blips.summary: Assess how a system may affect people and society before building it and again at each material change, and feed the results into the risk register.

blips.name: Controls enforced outside the model
blips.summary: Keep permissions, logging and a tested shutdown path in the harness around the model, not in its instructions, so an authorised person can always pause it mid-task.

blips.name: Shared AI incident disclosure
blips.summary: Disclose AI failures to those affected and share what failed, which controls broke and how to prevent it. The mechanisms for sharing across organisations are not yet established.

blips.name: Human approval as the only safeguard
blips.summary: Automation erodes the skills and attention people need to supervise it and take over when it fails. Pair human review with controls and evidence that do not depend on it.

blips.name: Shifting accountability to the model or provider
blips.summary: A tribunal held an airline liable for its chatbot's advice, and provider assurances do not transfer responsibility. Plan as though every AI output is the organisation's own statement.

blips.name: Capturing prompts and outputs by default
blips.summary: The OpenTelemetry conventions make content capture opt-in and warn it is likely to contain personal data. Enable it only under a written policy with an owner, retention and access controls.
